## Summary

Pipeline acceptance SHALL be defined at the user-visible rendering layer, not the database-write layer. A `make run` that completes all derivation targets SHALL NOT be considered successful unless every dashboard tab, for every active platform and product_line, renders content that satisfies declared per-element contracts (KPI value thresholds, DataTable meaningful row counts excluding placeholders, Plotly trace counts, filter dropdown choice counts). Hard fail at the DRV-end lite gate (NULL output detection) and at the deploy-gate full gate (every-field contract suite) prevents silent failures where the database is correctly populated but the user sees an empty dashboard.

## Motivation

GitHub issue #599 (filed 2026-05-10 as a meta-issue spawned from #595): during `/idd-implement #595` close session, the user observed that `#595` Phase A/B/C ship completed all of:

- `app_config.yaml database.mode` corrected from `duckdb` to `auto` (3 PRs across QEF_DESIGN, deploy bundle, D_RACING)
- `dbConnect_universal()` fail-loud regression test suite (locks against silent-create-empty-db reliance)
- `preflight_deploy_check.R` blocking deploy-time configuration mismatches
- `check_production_data.R` HTTP smoke against deployed Connect Cloud URL

…and yet the user could still locally reproduce QEF BrandEdge dashboard with no data when launching `Rscript app.R` from `l4_enterprise/QEF_DESIGN/`. The Phase A/B/C verification chain was correct in its narrow scope (deploy mode, db connection, HTTP availability) but missed the actual user-reported bug class — UI-layer rendering failure (3 distinct root causes in this case: hardcoded English empty-state, AI scoring data gap producing 50/54 NA-attribute rows, and `translate()` non-vectorized triggering "the condition has length > 1" red error).

> User observation that triggered this principle (2026-05-10):
>
> 「你可以說你是怎麼確認資料都會出現在儀表版上呢?就是我現在其實還先不用部署就看到 QEF 沒正常顯示了」
>
> 「test 必須檢視每一個欄位的數值」、「shinytest2 的 e2e 完整的 test」、「這些 test 是不是應該加入在 drv 的最後…這是原本 drv 需要補充的東西(也需要進入 principle)」

The implicit architectural commitment — "pipeline complete means dashboard-visible to the user" — was missing. MP162 covers this axis at the per-bridge L4 level (at least one Shiny module renders > 0 rows), but the per-dashboard-tab × per-platform × per-product_line granularity needed by `#595` is finer. MP163 covers a different axis entirely (input-completeness, not rendering-acceptance). MP165 fills the gap.

## Principle Statement

> A pipeline run SHALL be considered successful only when, for every active platform and active product_line in the company configuration, every dashboard tab declared in the per-company contract YAML renders content satisfying every contract assertion. Database-write completion is necessary but not sufficient. Failure to meet rendering acceptance SHALL halt the pipeline (DRV-end gate) or refuse the deploy (deploy gate).

The principle decomposes into three contract tiers, layered for performance, plus the framework primitives that enforce them.

## Two-Axis Acceptance Framework (v1.1, 2026-05-13)

The principle SHALL be applied along two orthogonal axes — **quality** (what to verify) and **context** (where to verify with what stringency). Both axes must hold for pipeline acceptance.

### Quality Axis

- **Step 1: No Red Errors** — every user-visible error count SHALL be zero:
  - Zero R `stop()` / uncaught errors propagating to the Shiny output area
  - Zero `[DEBUG_MODE_NULL_OUTPUT]` markers in `.shiny-debug/shiny.log`
  - Zero red error text strings rendered in the UI (e.g., "the condition has length > 1")
  - Zero JavaScript console errors during the default sidebar navigation walk
- **Step 2: Meaningful Values** — every user-visible value SHALL be informative:
  - KPI cards show numeric values satisfying declared `op` / `threshold`
  - DataTables show ≥ `min_rows` rows AFTER excluding placeholder rows (`Ideal`, `Rating`, `Revenue`)
  - Plotly charts show ≥ `min_traces` non-empty data arrays
  - Filter dropdowns expose ≥ `min_choices` valid choices
  - No card shows `-` / `NULL` / `NA` placeholder where a real value is expected

Step 1 is necessary but not sufficient for Step 2: a tab that renders zero errors but displays `-` for every KPI passes Step 1 and fails Step 2.

### Context Axis

- **Local check** (dev-time) — invoked during interactive development:
  - Tools: `Rscript app.R` + agent-browser snapshots + console grep
  - Stringency: `severity: critical` SHALL still fail loudly; `severity: warning` SHALL be reported but MAY allow developer to continue iterating
  - Cadence: developer-driven; recommended before each commit AND after each branch switch
  - Purpose: catch regressions cheaply during the edit-compile-test cycle
- **Deploy check** (pre-deploy gate) — invoked before `make deploy-push`:
  - Tools: `shared/global_scripts/23_deployment/dashboard_presence_gate.R`
  - Stringency: any `severity: critical` failure SHALL refuse the deploy push (non-zero exit). `severity: warning` reported but does not block.
  - Cadence: every deploy; required gate
  - Purpose: prevent production from regressing to a state the local check would have caught

The two contexts use the **same** per-company contract YAML and the **same** primitive helpers in `contracts.R`. The difference is stringency and runtime budget, NOT contract content.

### The 2×2 Matrix

|                  | Step 1: No Red Errors                                                | Step 2: Meaningful Values                                                          |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Local check**  | dev `Rscript app.R` console + browser console: zero red errors / zero `[DEBUG_MODE_NULL_OUTPUT]` | dev-time spot-check: KPI / DataTable show non-placeholder informative values        |
| **Deploy check** | `dashboard_presence_gate.R` refuses deploy on any `no_red_error_text` critical fail | `dashboard_presence_gate.R` refuses deploy on any `assert_*meaningful*` critical fail |

The 2×2 cells correspond to **deliverable verification artifacts**, not to disjoint code paths.

## Tier ↔ Step Mapping (v1.1)

The Tier system (1 / 2 / 3) describes **when** the check runs (implementation timing); the Step system (1 / 2) describes **what** the check verifies (quality criterion). They are NOT one-to-one.

| MP165 Tier (timing)                | Step 1 covered?                                  | Step 2 covered?                                          | Primary context |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| Tier 1 lite (DRV-end)              | YES (`[DEBUG_MODE_NULL_OUTPUT]` marker scan)      | NO (only checks NULL outputs, not values)                | Local-ish (dev + CI both run it) |
| Tier 2 full (deploy-gate)          | YES (`no_red_error_text` assertion across all UI) | YES (KPI threshold + DataTable rows + Plotly + dropdowns) | Deploy (strict) |
| Tier 3 CI selective (per PR)       | YES (per-module subset)                          | YES (per-module subset)                                  | CI (PR-scoped)  |

Implications:

- **Step 1 is NOT a single-Tier task**: `no_red_error_text` assertion appears in Tier 2 and Tier 3 contracts too. `[DEBUG_MODE_NULL_OUTPUT]` is the Tier 1 fast signal, but deploy-gate re-verifies it.
- **Step 2 is NOT a deploy-only task**: Local check SHALL include Step 2 spot-checks even though dev-time stringency is softer than deploy-gate stringency.
- **The 2×2 framework lives at the principle layer**, the Tier system lives at the implementation layer. Future contract primitives may serve either Step 1 or Step 2 (or both) and may run in any Tier.

## Local Check Discipline (v1.1)

Local check SHALL adhere to the same contract YAML and primitive helpers as deploy check, with two stringency relaxations and one cadence expectation.

### Stringency Relaxations

1. **Warning tolerance**: `severity: warning` contract failures during local check SHALL be reported (e.g., console log) but SHALL NOT halt the dev session.
2. **Optional `--severity-mode soft` flag** (when implemented in `run_smoke_lite.R` or a dedicated `run_local_check.R`): downgrades critical failures to warnings for the local context ONLY. This flag SHALL NOT exist on `dashboard_presence_gate.R` (deploy-gate hard-fail discipline is non-negotiable).

### Cadence

- Recommended: run local check before each commit AND after each branch switch.
- Required for fail-loud branches: when working on shared utilities consumed by all modules (e.g., `fn_translation.R`), local check SHALL run the full contract suite (mirrors Tier 3 reverse-dependency triggering).

### Tools

- Primary: `nohup Rscript app.R` + `agent-browser` snapshots + console grep (per backbone choice in Tier 1/2 sections).
- Diagnostic: `safari-browser` for live URL post-deploy verification (macOS only; native Safari, supports tab locking).
- Forbidden in local check: `shinytest2` AppDriver for dashboard-level walks (per backbone amendment from `#604`/`#605`).

### Distinction From Deploy Check

| Aspect          | Local check                                       | Deploy check                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Trigger         | Developer-initiated                                | Automatic before `make deploy-push`                  |
| Stringency      | Warnings tolerated; critical still fail-loud      | Any critical fail blocks deploy; warnings reported  |
| Runtime budget  | Best-effort (developer's call)                    | ≤ 60s hard ceiling per company                       |
| Failure action  | Developer fixes and re-runs                       | Pipeline aborts; deploy refused                      |
| Coverage scope  | Full or partial (developer's choice)              | Full contract suite for every active platform / PL   |

## Dual-Track Architecture (v1.2, 2026-05-13)

v1.2 codifies the long-implicit separation between two complementary tracks of dashboard rendering acceptance, both of which contribute to MP165 conformance:

### Track A: Declarative Baseline (existing)

Hand-maintained `qef_design.yaml` / `d_racing.yaml` / `mamba.yaml` / `wiser.yaml` / `kitchenmama.yaml` contract files, paired with the `contracts.R` primitive library + `dashboard_presence_gate.R` runner. Authors explicitly declare every selector and assertion. Auditable, deterministic, version-controlled. **Floor** of dashboard testing — what we know we want to test.

Properties:
- Closed-world coverage: only declared selectors evaluated
- Reproducible CI / deploy-gate behavior
- Hand-maintained — coverage growth proportional to author effort

### Track B: Adaptive Overlay (new, v1.2)

The `/shiny-adaptive-walk` skill (in `r-shiny-debugger` plugin v1.1+) executes a self-converging loop that discovers defects beyond the declarative baseline. Each iteration:

1. Walks the dashboard via safari-browser (real macOS renderer = user ground truth)
2. LLM judge classifies each visible defect: `real_bug` / `test_infra_gap` / `acceptable`
3. Bifurcated action:
   - `real_bug` → file `/idd-issue` (skill does NOT touch production code)
   - `test_infra_gap` → skill auto-mutates Track A files (yaml / primitives / walker)
4. Per-iter safety gate (test_dir + mechanical gate) + auto-rollback on regression
5. Convergence: CONVERGED / PLATEAUED / DIMINISHING (mirrors MP102 v1.3 `/glue-bridge` pattern)

**Ceiling** of dashboard testing — what we should test that we don't know to test yet.

Properties:
- Open-world coverage: walker discovers leaf sub-tabs + LLM judge surfaces unknown defects
- Skill mutations are observable via git diff (each iter = one commit)
- Coverage growth via convergence loop, bounded by `MP165_ADAPTIVE_BUDGET` LLM call cap

### (C) Aggressive Test-Framework Authority

Track B operates under **(C) Aggressive authority** over the test framework — skill MAY edit any file in the **mutable zone**:

- `shared/global_scripts/98_test/e2e/contracts/*.yaml`
- `shared/global_scripts/98_test/e2e/contracts/contracts.R`
- `shared/global_scripts/98_test/e2e/run_smoke_lite.R`
- `shared/global_scripts/98_test/e2e/test-*.R`
- `shared/global_scripts/23_deployment/dashboard_presence_gate.R`
- `shared/global_scripts/04_utils/fn_debug_mode.R`

Skill **MUST NOT** edit any file in the **immutable zone** (files `/idd-issue` instead):

- `shared/global_scripts/10_rshinyapp_components/**` (UI components)
- `shared/global_scripts/16_derivations/**` (business logic)
- `shared/global_scripts/04_utils/fn_analysis_*.R` (analysis functions)
- `shared/update_scripts/ETL/**`, `shared/update_scripts/DRV/**` (pipelines)
- Any `.qmd` principle file (human-only decision)

Pre-mutation glob check is hard-coded in the skill spec. Mutation attempt against immutable zone is a skill bug.

### Track convergence

The two tracks are complementary, not competitive:

- Track B discovers a defect → files issue (`real_bug`) OR adds contract to Track A `# === auto-suggested ===` block (`test_infra_gap`)
- Track A contracts evaluated by `dashboard_presence_gate.R` — Track B's mechanical regression step
- Hand-maintained sections of yaml are immutable to Track B (sister to MP159 Layer 1 immutability for glue authoring)

**Declarative is the floor; adaptive is the ceiling.** Both axes must hold for full MP165 conformance.

## DRV-Layer Step 2 Propagation (v1.3, 2026-05-14)

v1.1 introduced **Step 2 "Meaningful Values"** as a quality-axis acceptance criterion enforced at the dashboard layer (KPI > threshold, DataTable rows ≥ min excluding placeholders, Plotly traces non-empty, dropdowns ≥ min_choices). v1.2 added the dual-track architecture (Track A declarative + Track B adaptive) for that dashboard-layer enforcement. **v1.3 propagates Step 2 to the DRV layer.**

### The vacuous-pass gap that motivated v1.3

The dashboard-layer Step 2 gate catches DRV vacuous-pass cases (DRV pipeline reports success producing empty / partial output tables) only *after* the user navigates to the affected sub-tab. Three concrete cases discovered in 2026-05-13 cross-company adaptive walk (issue [#668](https://github.com/kiki830621/ai_martech_global_scripts/issues/668)):

- **D_RACING amz**: `df_amz_poisson_analysis_all` table does not exist (DRV never invoked) — dashboard renders graceful empty state, but pipeline reported full success.
- **QEF_DESIGN amz**: `df_amz_poisson_analysis_all` exists with 189 rows but ONLY `predictor_type = time_feature` (no `comment_attribute` / `product_attribute` rows). Dashboard InsightForge sub-tabs that depend on the non-time predictor types render `--` placeholders.
- **MAMBA cbz**: same predictor_type-distribution issue, 65 rows but missing required types.

All three cases pass the dashboard's Step 1 "No Red Errors" (no `Error:` text, no `[DEBUG_MODE_NULL_OUTPUT]` from the empty-state UI path) yet violate Step 2 "Meaningful Values" — and the violation is *upstream of* the dashboard, in the DRV output shape itself. The dashboard layer is the wrong enforcement point for this defect class.

### The v1.3 normative addition

DRV pipelines SHALL invoke an output-shape gate as the final pipeline target. The gate SHALL verify each declared DRV output at three levels:

- **L1 table-exists** (mandatory): The named DuckDB table SHALL exist in `app_data.duckdb`.
- **L2 row-count-min** (mandatory): The table SHALL contain at least `l2_row_count_min` rows.
- **L3 predictor-type-distribution** (optional, where applicable): Tables with a `predictor_type` column SHALL contain at least `min_count_per_type` rows for each declared required predictor_type.

Contracts SHALL live in `shared/global_scripts/98_test/e2e/contracts/<company>_drv.yaml`, parallel to (and NOT inside) the existing dashboard `<company>.yaml`. The gate script `shared/global_scripts/23_deployment/drv_output_shape_gate.R` is independent from `dashboard_presence_gate.R` (different input source: DuckDB tables via DBI vs Shiny UI elements via headless browser) but SHARES the same `contracts.R` primitive library where applicable.

### Two-axis framework, restated for v1.3

| Quality axis | Enforcement layer | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Step 1: No Red Errors | Dashboard layer | `[DEBUG_MODE_NULL_OUTPUT]` scan + `no_red_error_text` assertion |
| **Step 2: Meaningful Values** | **DRV layer (NEW v1.3)** | **`drv_output_shape_gate.R` against `<company>_drv.yaml`** |
| Step 2: Meaningful Values | Dashboard layer (existing v1.1) | `assert_kpi_card_value` / `assert_datatable_meaningful_rows` / `assert_plotly_has_data_points` etc. |

Step 2 is enforced at *both* layers because the two layers fail in different ways. DRV-layer enforcement makes vacuous-pass impossible at the producer side. Dashboard-layer enforcement catches consumer-side regressions (e.g., DRV output is fine but Shiny module filters it out). Defense in depth.

### MP163 sentinel boundary

Sentinel-covered rows (`'unclassified'`, `'UNKNOWN'`, per-domain MP163 markers) SHALL count toward L2 and L3 by default. They are explicit gap markers per MP163 Progressive Completeness, not missing data. Rejecting sentinel rows would force pipelines to `stop()` when input is incomplete, directly contradicting MP163's "always runnable" tenet.

An optional `sentinel_ratio_max` per contract (default off) emits a *warning* when sentinel rows exceed a configurable fraction of total rows. This catches the case where sentinels mask a real upstream coverage problem without making the default behaviour incompatible with MP163.

### 30-day warn-mode transition

For 30 days after this v1.3 amendment merges (default sunset 2026-06-13), the gate operates in warn-mode by default: a missing `<company>_drv.yaml` for a registered pipeline emits a warning but SHALL NOT block `make run`. After sunset, the default flips to strict-mode: missing contracts SHALL cause hard-fail. Pattern matches MP102 v1.3's `reviewed_by` legacy-format sunset window (legacy accepted until 2026-07-31, then mandatory structured form). Per-company opt-in to strict-mode before sunset via `strict_mode: true` in `<company>_drv.yaml`.

### Why this is a v1.3 amendment, not a sibling MP166

v1.1 already framed Step 2 as a quality axis applicable across layers. The dashboard layer was the first instance; the DRV layer is the second. Conceptually they are the same principle enforced at different points, not different principles. A sibling MP166 would have identical Step 2 vocabulary and high cross-reference density — strong signal of one principle, two enforcement points. MP102 evolved similarly (v1.0 → v1.3, each amendment adding rigor without splitting).

## Tier 1: DRV-End Lite Check (NULL Output Detection)

`update_scripts/DRV/_targets.R` SHALL include a final target `dashboard_smoke_lite` that runs after all 5NM-layer derivations complete. The target SHALL launch a headless Shiny session in `SHINY_DEBUG_MODE=TRUE`, walk the default sidebar nav state across all active platforms and product_lines, and inspect the `.shiny-debug/shiny.log` for `[DEBUG_MODE_NULL_OUTPUT]` markers emitted by `04_utils/fn_debug_mode.R::debug_log_output()`.

Any NULL render output SHALL fail the target. The pipeline rebuild SHALL fail with a structured message identifying `(company, tab, platform, product_line, output_id)`.

**Runtime budget**: target ≤ 5 seconds typical, hard ceiling 30 seconds per company. Designed to be cheap enough for every `make run`.

## Tier 2: Deploy-Gate Full Contract Suite

`shared/global_scripts/23_deployment/dashboard_presence_gate.R` SHALL run before `make deploy-push` invokes `rsconnect`. The gate loads the per-company contract YAML at `shared/global_scripts/98_test/e2e/contracts/<company_lowercase>.yaml`, launches headless Shiny once per `(active_platform, active_product_line)` tuple, and evaluates every contract via the primitive helpers in `contracts.R`.

Any contract with `severity: critical` failing SHALL cause the gate to exit non-zero and refuse the deploy push. Contracts with `severity: warning` SHALL be reported but SHALL NOT block deploy.

**Runtime budget**: ≤ 60 seconds per company on typical app data sets. Acceptable because deploy is not a frequent operation.

## Tier 3: CI Selective per Pull Request

A CI workflow SHALL read the PR `git diff --name-only` between head and base, map changed paths to module identifiers via `shared/global_scripts/98_test/e2e/affected_modules.R`, and run only the corresponding contract subsets. The workflow SHALL complete within 30 seconds for typical PRs that touch one or two modules.

PRs touching shared utilities consumed by all modules (e.g., `fn_translation.R`) SHALL trigger the full contract suite — selectivity is by reverse-dependency, not by file alone.

## Contract Primitive Library

`shared/global_scripts/98_test/e2e/contracts/contracts.R` SHALL provide at minimum five per-element-type assertion primitives:

| Primitive                              | Asserts                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `assert_kpi_card_value`                | KPI card displays a value satisfying `op` (`>=`, `>`, `==`) against `threshold`         |
| `assert_datatable_meaningful_rows`     | DataTable has ≥ `min_rows` after excluding placeholder rows (`Ideal`, `Rating`, `Revenue`) |
| `assert_plotly_has_data_points`        | Plotly chart has ≥ `min_traces` traces with non-empty data arrays                       |
| `assert_filter_dropdown_choices`       | Filter selectize / dropdown populates ≥ `min_choices` valid choices                     |
| `assert_chart_axis_non_empty`          | Specified chart axis (`x` or `y`) has populated tick labels                             |

The primitives SHALL accept consistent signature `(app, selector_id, ..., severity = "critical")`.

The default `exclude_placeholders = TRUE` for `assert_datatable_meaningful_rows` is the critical strengthening of the prior weak `assert_datatable_has_rows(min_rows = 1)` contract — the prior contract incorrectly passed when QEF hsg had only 1 row (the `Ideal` placeholder), missing the actual data gap.

## Per-Company Contract YAML Schema

```yaml
company: <COMPANY_NAME>
modules:
  <module_name>:
    enabled: true | false
    sub_tabs:
      <tab_id>:
        active_product_lines: [<id>, ...]
        contracts:
          - selector: <ns_id>
            assertion: "<expression evaluated against the rendered output>"
            severity: critical | warning
```

Per-company YAML lives at `shared/global_scripts/98_test/e2e/contracts/<company_lowercase>.yaml`. Companies that do not enable a module (e.g., KITCHENMAMA without BrandEdge) SHALL set `enabled: false` for documentation, OR may omit the module entirely. The natural opt-out path is the absence of the corresponding DRV target in the company's `update_scripts/DRV/_targets.R` — declarative dependency ensures the contract target does not run when its source DRV is absent.

## Hard Fail Discipline

The framework SHALL NOT support a global `soft_warn_mode` toggle that downgrades all critical contracts to warnings. The only opt-out paths are:

1. The company does not enable the corresponding DRV (declarative dependency natural opt-out).
2. The contract is explicitly declared `severity: warning` in the YAML (Tier 2 reports but does not block deploy; Tier 1 ignores severity since Tier 1 only checks NULL outputs).

Hard fail aligns with the user requirement of "打通 + 不會紅字" (pipeline must work AND no red errors). Early fail-loud at the DRV gate prevents late red errors at the user's screen.

## Backbone Implementation: nohup Rscript + agent-browser (NOT shinytest2)

Tier 1 lite (`run_smoke_lite.R`) and Tier 2 deploy gate (`dashboard_presence_gate.R`) drive the company's Shiny app via:

```
nohup Rscript app.R > .shiny-debug/shiny.log 2>&1 &
agent-browser open http://127.0.0.1:<port>
agent-browser snapshot -i  # find element refs
agent-browser fill / click # auth + walk top-nav
# Read .shiny-debug/shiny.log for [DEBUG_MODE_NULL_OUTPUT] markers
```

This is intentionally **not** `shinytest2`. The choice was made empirically after `#604` and `#605` showed shinytest2's stability detector aborts on plotly-heavy initial renders even after the underlying reactive cross-tab leak (`#603`) was gated, and shinytest2's chromote subprocess writes to a temp dir not the `.shiny-debug/shiny.log` path that `04_utils/fn_debug_mode.R::debug_log_output()` writes to (DEV_R054).

**Constraints**:

- **Tier 1 lite**: deterministic agent-browser navigation timing; not subject to plotly stability detector races.
- **Tier 2 deploy gate**: same backbone as Tier 1; v2 evaluates NULL-output markers only (per-element DOM contracts deferred to v3 follow-up — DOM extraction helpers via `agent-browser snapshot --page`).
- **Tier 3 CI selective**: `affected_modules.R` selects subset; CI runs the same gate, agent-browser works in headless Chromium under GitHub Actions.

**`shinytest2` retained for `98_test/e2e/test-*.R` unit-style tests** (single-output value assertions). For DASHBOARD-LEVEL e2e (per-tab × per-platform × per-product_line walk), the Rscript + agent-browser backbone is the framework standard.

**Escape hatch in existing tests**: `test-brandedge.R` exposes `MP165_USE_AGENT_BROWSER=true` env var that delegates the L1 test to `run_smoke_lite.R`. Default keeps `shinytest2` for backward compatibility with CI workflows that already use it.

**Cross-platform note**: `agent-browser` is the primary tool (cross-platform Chromium via Puppeteer). `safari-browser` (macOS native Safari) is the alternative for live URL post-deploy verification (e.g., MAMBA Posit Connect Cloud). Both share the snapshot/click ref-based API, so any helper written against agent-browser can be re-pointed to safari-browser by changing the CLI binary name.

**IC_P002 cross-co verified 2026-05-10**: backbone tested PASS on QEF_DESIGN (119 contracts, 18.6s), D_RACING (13 contracts), MAMBA (10 contracts). Single shared `run_smoke_lite.R` + `dashboard_presence_gate.R` work for all 3 companies without per-company code changes.

## Anti-Patterns

| Anti-Pattern                                                  | Why Wrong                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `assert_datatable_has_rows(min_rows = 1)` without exclusion   | 1-row `Ideal` placeholder passes; misses the actual data gap                               |
| Adding `soft_warn_mode = TRUE` to skip failing contracts      | Defeats the gate; user requirement explicit "不會紅字" demands hard fail                     |
| Putting `enabled: false` on a module that has an active DRV   | Inconsistent state — DRV writes data but contracts skip; surfaces as deploy gate skip      |
| Running Tier 1 lite alone (skipping Tier 2 deploy gate)       | NULL detection is necessary but insufficient — every-field assertions catch the 1-row case |
| Hardcoding contract thresholds in R instead of company YAML   | Cross-company maintenance friction; QEF brand counts != D_RACING brand counts               |
| Skipping `IC_P002` cross-company verify on contract YAML      | Cross-company impact requires explicit verification per `IC_P002` discipline                |

## Compliant Patterns

| Compliant Pattern                                                                          | Why Correct                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `assert_datatable_meaningful_rows(min_rows = 5, exclude_placeholders = TRUE)`              | Catches the `Ideal`-only case from `#595` reproduction                                    |
| Tier 1 lite at DRV-end + Tier 2 full at deploy-gate (layered)                              | Performance budget respected (5s on every `make run`, 60s only on infrequent deploy)      |
| `severity: warning` on tabs not yet fully implemented                                      | Allows incremental rollout while still surfacing the gap                                  |
| KITCHENMAMA omits BrandEdge contracts entirely (relies on absent DRV target)               | Declarative dependency natural opt-out                                                    |
| Per-company YAML threshold (`min_brands: 5` for QEF, `min_brands: 3` for D_RACING)          | Company-specific tuning without R code change                                             |
| Contract YAML loader validates schema at startup with actionable error                     | Surfaces typos before contract execution                                                  |

### Change Discipline

Modifications to bound files SHALL respect:

- `IC_P002` cross-company verification (5 companies must verify): commit message includes `Verified:` trailer
- `DOC_R009` triple-layer sync: any spec/threshold/principle change updates `.qmd` (Layer 1, this file) → `llm/*.yaml` (Layer 2) → `.claude/rules/*.md` (Layer 3) in that order
- `MP029` verify-before-acting: contract additions SHALL be motivated by an actual reproduction case, not speculation

## Sister Principle Cross-References

### MP162 as the per-bridge complement

MP162 governs the per-bridge ship-readiness axis (L1-L5). MP162 L4 requires at least one Shiny module to render > 0 rows for the bridge's downstream data. MP165 is the per-dashboard-tab × per-platform × per-product_line complement — finer granularity, broader unit. Both must hold for production-ready data flow.

### MP163 as the orthogonal complement

MP163 governs the input-completeness axis: the pipeline keeps running when human inputs are absent, gaps surface as sentinels. MP165 governs the rendering-acceptance axis: the pipeline only succeeds when every tab × platform × product_line renders contract-pass content. The two are orthogonal — both axes must hold for user-facing completeness. A pipeline can satisfy MP163 (gracefully sentinel-bucket gaps) yet fail MP165 (those gaps render as user-visible empty tabs that surface no actionable hint), and vice versa.

### MP102 v1.3 as the upstream contract layer

MP102 v1.3 governs bridge yaml authoring contract (reviewed_by structured, sibling review log, four-agent self-converging review). MP165 is downstream: bridge yaml correct + DRV pipeline complete is necessary but not sufficient for user-visible completeness. The rendering layer needs its own acceptance contract.

### MP029 as the verify-before-acting alignment

MP029 demands verify-before-acting against fake information. MP165 contract assertions are concrete reproductions: a 1-row `Ideal` placeholder is observably-empty even if the row count is technically ≥ 1. The strengthened `assert_datatable_meaningful_rows` primitive operationalizes MP029 at the rendering boundary.

## Change Log

### v1.3 (2026-05-14) — DRV-Layer Step 2 Propagation

GitHub issue: [#668](https://github.com/kiki830621/ai_martech_global_scripts/issues/668)

**Architectural amendment + new section, propagates Step 2 "Meaningful Values" enforcement from the dashboard layer to the DRV layer.**

What changed:

- **New section: DRV-Layer Step 2 Propagation** — explicit codification of Step 2 quality axis enforcement at the DRV layer via a new `drv_output_shape_gate.R` script and per-company `<company>_drv.yaml` contracts. Closes the vacuous-pass gap where DRV pipelines reported success producing empty / partial output tables (3 concrete cases: D_RACING amz missing table, QEF amz incomplete predictor_type distribution, MAMBA cbz same pattern).
- **3-level granularity formalization**: L1 table-exists (mandatory) + L2 row-count-min (mandatory) + L3 predictor-type-distribution (optional, where applicable). Two-level alone is too coarse — empty time_feature would also be missed.
- **MP163 sentinel-cover boundary** — sentinels count toward L2 and L3 by default (don't break Progressive Completeness); optional `sentinel_ratio_max` warning for opt-in detection of mask-by-sentinel anti-pattern.
- **30-day warn-mode transition** — default warn-mode until 2026-06-13 sunset, then strict-mode; per-company `strict_mode: true` opt-in available before sunset. Matches MP102 v1.3's `reviewed_by` legacy-format sunset pattern.

What did NOT change (backward compatibility):

- All v1.0 / v1.1 / v1.2 sections continue to apply unchanged.
- All existing Track A contract yamls (`qef_design.yaml` / `d_racing.yaml` / `mamba.yaml`) continue to work — they govern dashboard-layer enforcement, orthogonal to the new DRV-layer yaml.
- All existing `contracts.R` primitives continue to work — the new gate uses DBI direct queries, shares the primitive library only where applicable.
- Track B (`/shiny-adaptive-walk`) continues to govern dashboard-layer adaptive overlay — the DRV gate is a separate axis.

**Why now**: 2026-05-13 cross-company adaptive walk (issue #653 Phase 5) surfaced systematic vacuous-pass at the DRV layer across multiple companies. Per `/spectra-discuss` convergence, 6 design decisions locked:

1. MP165 v1.3 amendment (NOT sibling MP166)
2. Independent `drv_output_shape_gate.R` (NOT `dashboard_presence_gate.R --mode drv`)
3. Standalone `<company>_drv.yaml` per company (NOT in `app_config.yaml`)
4. 3-level granularity (L1 + L2 + L3 optional)
5. 30-day warn-mode → strict-mode transition
6. MP163 sentinels pass by default; `sentinel_ratio_max` opt-in warning

**Triple-layer sync** (per DOC_R009):

- Layer 1 .qmd (en + zh): this file + zh mirror
- Layer 2 `llm/CH00_meta.yaml`: MP165 entry `version: 1.3` with DRV-layer Step 2 vocabulary in `one_liner` + new `rule_natural` sub-rule
- Layer 3 `.claude/rules/01-always.md`: MP165 quick reference appended DRV-layer gate (v1.3) sentence

**Spectra change**: `mp165-drv-output-shape-gate` (`openspec/changes/mp165-drv-output-shape-gate/`, 5-phase tasks file). v1.3 amendment is Phase 1 of that change.

### v1.2 (2026-05-13) — Dual-Track Architecture + Aggressive Test-Framework Authority

GitHub issue: [#653](https://github.com/kiki830621/ai_martech_global_scripts/issues/653)

**Architectural amendment + new section, codifies Track A / Track B / (C) authority for the new `/shiny-adaptive-walk` skill**.

What changed:

- **New section: Dual-Track Architecture** — explicit codification of Track A (declarative baseline,existing) + Track B (adaptive overlay,new `/shiny-adaptive-walk` skill). Previously Track A existed but was the only track;Track B added without principle backing would have been ad-hoc.
- **(C) Aggressive authority specification** — explicit mutable-zone whitelist for Track B skill to edit test framework + immutable-zone blacklist (production code) routed to `/idd-issue` instead.
- **Track convergence prose** — declarative is the floor, adaptive is the ceiling. Both must hold for full MP165 conformance.

What did NOT change (backward compatibility):

- All existing Track A contracts (`qef_design.yaml` / `d_racing.yaml` / `mamba.yaml`) continue to work unchanged
- All existing contract primitives in `contracts.R` continue to work (+ 3 new from Phase 1: `assert_no_error_text`、`assert_no_hardcoded_english`、`assert_kpi_no_error_placeholder`)

The 5 defects are real bugs;the gate gap is a coverage-completeness gap. Track B is the architectural response that lets adaptive discovery close coverage gaps without violating Track A's hand-maintained authoritative status.

### v1.1 (2026-05-13) — Two-Axis Step 1/Step 2 × Local/Deploy Framework

GitHub issue: [#648](https://github.com/kiki830621/ai_martech_global_scripts/issues/648)

**Vocabulary amendment, no normative behavior change**. The existing Tier 1/2/3 contract enforcement remains unchanged. v1.1 adds explicit two-axis vocabulary that was previously implicit:

- **New section: Two-Axis Acceptance Framework** — separates the quality axis (Step 1: no red errors / Step 2: meaningful values) from the context axis (Local check / Deploy check).
- **New section: Tier ↔ Step Mapping** — disambiguation table clarifying that Tier 1 is not equivalent to Step 1; Tier system is timing, Step system is quality criterion.
- **New section: Local Check Discipline** — explicit local context spec (warning tolerance, severity relaxations, cadence) differentiated from deploy-gate hard-fail discipline.

**Rationale**: prior to v1.1, the Step 1 / Step 2 quality criteria were embedded inside contract primitive function semantics (`assert_kpi_card_value` implicitly = Step 2; `no_red_error_text` implicitly = Step 1) without principle-level codification. The local vs. deploy stringency distinction was implicit in the "Hard Fail Discipline" section but not differentiated as orthogonal context axis. v1.1 elevates both axes to first-class principle vocabulary so future verification work can mechanically align (e.g., "this issue verifies Step 2 in Local context for QEF amz dashboard").

**Backward compatibility**: all existing contract YAMLs (`qef_design.yaml`, `d_racing.yaml`, `mamba.yaml`), all existing primitive helpers in `contracts.R`, and all existing Tier 1/2/3 runners (`run_smoke_lite.R`, `dashboard_presence_gate.R`) continue to work unchanged. The amendment is purely additive at the principle layer.

**Triple-layer sync** (per DOC_R009):

- Layer 1 .qmd (en + zh): this file + zh mirror
- Layer 2 `llm/CH00_meta.yaml`: MP165 entry updated to `version: 1.1` with Two-Axis vocabulary in `one_liner` and new `rule_natural` sub-rule (6)
- Layer 3 `.claude/rules/01-always.md`: MP165 quick reference appended Two-Axis (v1.1) sentence
